value.produces: assets/mvs38/{tk5,rootfs} — the pinned TK5 distribution of MVS 3.8j (its own SDL Hyperion Hercules, the DASD volumes, conf/ and scripts/), made executable, plus the container rootfs (relaunch reset). Nothing is built from source: the TK5 zip is the artifact, pinned by size and SHA-256 in assets/mvs38/MANIFEST.sha256.

labctl.notes: EMULATED MACHINE, CONTAINED, NO CHECKPOINT: Hercules runs IBM MVS 3.8j (the TK5 distribution) inside a systemd-nspawn container together with the station's Xvfb and one x3270; the daemon captures the X root (SH_CAPTURE=x11) and types over XTEST (SH_INPUT_BACKEND=x11test). There is no pointer — a 3270 data stream carries none. No QMP and no exec channel: `labctl shot` reads the X root. The visitor terminal is VTAM local device 00C0 on the CONTAINER's loopback CNSLPORT 3270, so it claims no host port and is unreachable from labhost; to drive the guest by hand, enter the container's netns — `nsenter -t $(cat /data/vms/streamhost/stations/mvs38/mame.pid) -n c3270 127.0.0.1:3270` — and only while no visitor is attached. mame.pid is the Hercules HOST pid (idle freezer and reap-by-exe), nspawn.pid the supervisor. THE MVS OPERATOR CONSOLE IS NOT THE MUSEUM SURFACE and is not on a 3270 at all: TK5CONS=intcons puts it on device 0009 3215-C, an integrated console whose whole traffic goes to work/emulator.log. That is also where the readiness gate reads `IKT005I TCAS IS INITIALIZED` — the CNSLPORT listener opens 39 s earlier and means nothing. Reset=relaunch: kill Hercules by mame.pid, wipe work/, rebuild work/tk5 from the read-only TK5 tree and start again. Launcher stations/mvs38/x11-runtime.sh, which execs the lane's shared engine docs/lab/record-wave/shared-terminal-runtime.sh; assets in assets/mvs38 (MANIFEST.sha256 pins the upstream zip).

render.bindingComment: ideal: an IBM System/370 frame in a raised-floor machine room with an IBM 3279 colour display terminal on a desk in front of it

pointer.device: none — a 1986 Berkeley timesharing terminal has no pointing device, and 4.3BSD's tty line carries none. The x11test backend is present for KEYS only (SH_X11TEST_KEYS=1).

spa.eraLabel: 1981 · IBM MVS 3.8j — the mainframe behind the green screen

museum.lineage: OS/360 → OS/VS2 SVS (1972) → MVS (1974) → MVS 3.8j → MVS/XA → MVS/ESA → OS/390 → z/OS
museum.arch: IBM System/370 as Hercules configures it for TK5 — an IBM 3033-class processor, S/370 architecture level, one CPU and 16 MiB of main storage, with 3390, 3380 and 3350 DASD, a 3211 line printer, a 3505 card reader, a 3525 punch, a 3420 tape drive and eight local 3270 display stations on the VTAM channel
eraSoftware: TSO — the Time Sharing Option, the interactive front end to a batch machine
ISPF and its editor — the full-screen panels every mainframe programmer lived in
JES2, the job entry subsystem: SUBMIT, the spool, and the held output queue
JCL — //STEP EXEC PGM=IEFBR14, the language for asking a mainframe to do anything
the OS utilities: IEBGENER, IEBCOPY, IEHLIST, IDCAMS, SORT
COBOL, PL/I, FORTRAN and OS/360 Assembler F, all under the same JCL
BREXX/370 — a modern REXX brought back to a 1981 machine
RAKF, the turnkey security manager that guards the TSO userids
museum.periodBrowser: none — MVS 3.8j is a 1981 batch and timesharing system with no TCP/IP stack at all. Its network was SNA and RJE, and this exhibit is deliberately not networked: the 3270 terminal is the whole visitor surface.
museum.blurb: The machine the phrase 'the mainframe' still means. MVS is what IBM's System/370 ran in the banks, airlines and government departments of the late 1970s and 1980s, and MVS 3.8j is the last release IBM ever put into the public domain — which is why it is the one release anybody can still boot. Everything here is the real thing: you sit at a 3270, a block-mode terminal that sends nothing until you press Enter, log on to TSO, and find ISPF, JCL and JES2 exactly as a 1981 systems programmer did. It is a strikingly alien computer to meet after forty years of glass teletypes — the screen is a form you fill in, work is submitted as jobs rather than run, and the machine answers with a message number you are expected to look up. It is also the direct ancestor of z/OS, still running under most of the world's card transactions today.
museum.notes: Tier 3, EMULATED but CONTAINED and with no checkpoint: Hercules, the station's Xvfb and the visitor's x3270 all run inside one systemd-nspawn container (private PID/mount/net/IPC/UTS/user namespaces, uid base 2097152, volatile overlay root, the TK5 tree bound read-only, CAP_SYS_ADMIN dropped). MVS 3.8j is 1981 software with no security model worth the name, so the container — not the guest — is the boundary. The visitor surface is one IBM 3279 colour display on VTAM local device 00C0; the MVS operator console is device 0009 3215-C (TK5CONS=intcons) and goes to the Hercules log, never to a 3270 and never on screen. The exhibit logs itself on to TSO at bring-up and rests on the ISPF primary option menu — MVS reaches neither on its own, because a 3270 sends nothing until an AID key is pressed and VTAM says nothing until it is spoken to. No checkpoint: reset is a ~103 s relaunch from the pristine TK5 DASD volumes, which are bound read-only and are byte-identical to a fresh unzip of the pinned archive. See docs/guests/mvs38.md.

emulator.version: SDL Hyperion Hercules 4.8, the build TK5 bundles for linux/64 (hercules/linux/64/bin/hercules)
emulator.source: The TK5 turnkey distribution of MVS 3.8j by Rob Prins, mvs-tk5.zip, 498312872 bytes, sha256 710d002843631322810a276dd42c793fda458548dc64d86e2914a62db7425f84; staged by scripts/build-guests/tiles/mvs38.sh and pinned in assets/mvs38/MANIFEST.sha256. The zip carries its own Hercules — Debian's hercules 3.13 will not run this configuration — and ships everything mode 0644, so the builder must chmod +x it.
emulator.driver: tk5 (conf/tk5.cnf, CPUMODEL 3033, ARCHLVL S/370, MAINSIZE 16, NUMCPU 1)

network.note: No network plane at all. MVS 3.8j has no TCP/IP: its networking was SNA/VTAM and RJE, neither of which reaches anything a visitor could see. Hercules’ own CNSLPORT (3270) and HTTP server (8038) bind the CONTAINER’s loopback behind --private-network, so they claim no host port and are unreachable from labhost.

reset.mouse: N/A — no pointing device. A 3270 is a block-mode terminal: it carries typed fields and AID keys and nothing else, and the exhibit publishes no pointer (stream.pointer.present=false).
reset.keyboard: PASS (2026-09-20) — XTEST keys reach the guest through the container's Xvfb, and the 3270 AID keys arrive as AID keys, not as text. On the live rig at the ISPF primary option menu: F1 produced ISPF's HELP response, F3 produced END and dropped the session to TSO's `READY` prompt, typing `ISPF` brought the menu back, and Alt+C cleared the screen and unlocked the keyboard. The mapping is not x3270's defaults: it is a keymap committed in stations/mvs38/nspawn-inner.sh and matched key-for-key by the SPA's `tn3270` on-screen keyboard profile. TRAPS: (1) no window manager runs in the container, so X focus is PointerRoot and XTEST keys go to the root window and vanish unless the launcher pins focus with xdotool windowfocus — it does, once, at bring-up; (2) x3270 finds a keymap ONLY as an X resource — `-keymap <file>` and a file in $HOME/.x3270 both answer `Cannot find keymap`; (3) XK_Pause, the key a desktop tn3270 client would give Clear, is not in guestQuirks.keysymToScancode, so it would have shipped as a silently dead button — Clear rides Alt+C instead.
reset.fixture: One IBM 3279-2-E colour display, x3270 with the bitmap font 3270-20 (821x513 px, centred at +101+127), on an otherwise black 1024x768 Xvfb root — the whole station is that one terminal. No menu bar and no keypad: they are host chrome a visitor cannot click (this station publishes no pointer) and they crop the 24x80 screen. THE REST SCENE IS THE ISPF PRIMARY OPTION MENU, logged on as the TSO userid in the station fixture, showing the numbered option list (BROWSE, EDIT, RPF, UTILITIES, FOREGROUND, BATCH, COMMAND, DIALOG TEST, TUTORIAL, TK5) and a status block reading USERID, TIME, TERMINAL 3277, PANEL ISP@PRIM, RELEASE V2.2.000, SYSTEMID TK5R, PROC ISPLOGON. MVS does not get there by itself and neither does a bare client: Hercules paints its own device logo, a 3270's fields on it are PROTECTED so typing only locks the keyboard with X SYSTEM, and VTAM answers nothing until it is spoken to. stations/mvs38/x3270-session.sh therefore drives Clear -> `TSO` -> userid -> password -> the `***` pages through x3270's OWN scripting interface, gating every step on the screen text (Ascii()), never on a sleep, and writes work/logon.ok only when `ISPF primary option menu` is actually on the screen. THE HERCULES DEVICE LOGO IS REPLACED: the stock TK5 herclogo.txt prints $(VERSION), $(HOSTNAME), $(HOSTOS), $(HOSTARCH), $(HOSTNUMCPUS) and $(LPARNAME) at the top of the first screen a 3270 ever sees — the emulator's version and the host's name, kernel and core count, on the museum's own framebuffer. The committed replacement keeps TK5's artwork and credits and only the device number and subchannel. Bring-up gates on TWO things, because neither alone is enough: work/logon.ok for WHICH screen, and a framebuffer lit-pixel floor of 20000 for whether there is a screen at all. MEASURED: ISPF menu 32512 lit px, Hercules logo 27811, a blank 3270 with one message 5747-6575 — and 25765 for the first build of this station, which was a completely blank 3270 under x3270's menu bar and would have passed a naive floor. resetMode=relaunch with no statefile: kill Hercules by mame.pid, wipe work/, rebuild work/tk5 (symlinks to the read-only tree for the inert 254 MB; real copies of dasd/ and the spool dirs, ~1.2 s because /data is ZFS with block cloning active) and start again — ~103 s to the ISPF menu at load 45, of which Hercules exec to `IKT005I TCAS IS INITIALIZED` is 55 s and the scripted logon a further 17 s. PROVEN 2026-09-20: `ALLOC DA(VISITOR.TEST) NEW CATALOG` in the guest, `LISTDS` showed HERC01.VISITOR.TEST on volume TSO003; after a relaunch the same LISTDS answered `DATA SET HERC01.VISITOR.TEST NOT IN CATALOG`, and the seed's DASD volumes hash identical to a fresh unzip of the pinned archive. Idle standby PROVEN too: Hercules SIGSTOPped for 180 s (state T) and SIGCONTed, after which TSO answered `TIME` normally.

notes: Record wave 2026-09-20, Lane B (docs/lab/MVS38-WAVE.md): the station that measured the readiness finding behind docs/lab/record-wave/shared-terminal-runtime.sh — a TCP port probe is not a readiness gate — and the first station in the lane to run a mainframe rather than a minicomputer.
